metadata.title: Meta Faces a Potential $1.4 Trillion Legal Test

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Meta Platforms Inc. (META, Financials), the parent of Facebook and Instagram, is heading into its biggest youth social media trial yet, with potential damages the company says could reach as high as $1.4 trillion.
The trial begins Wednesday in California and involves claims from 29 states that Meta illegally collected children's data and designed its platforms to keep younger users hooked.
The financial risk is only part of the story. States are also asking the court to impose nationwide changes, including age restrictions, strict time limits for younger users and the elimination of features such as infinite scroll.
They also want Meta to alter recommendation systems so they prioritize well-being rather than engagement. That could matter far more to investors than a one-time fine.
Facebook and Instagram depend heavily on engagement to support advertising revenue. Changes that reduce how long users spend on the platforms could eventually affect monetization.
CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Instagram chief Adam Mosseri are expected to testify. For investors, this trial is becoming a test not only of Meta's legal exposure, but of how much courts may be willing to reshape its core products.
